rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Insecticides, herbicides, fungicides and rodenticides are the classes. DDT, BHC, malathion and 2,4-D are the names to place.
Non-target death includes bees and the predators that had been eating the pest.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Insecticide kills insects, herbicide kills weeds, fungicide kills fungi — match the suffix to the target.  ·  Biomagnification is concentration rising UP the food chain; bioaccumulation is build-up within one body.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Keep the course example attached to the right class.  ·  A direction word (to sea, to fresh water, in-situ, ex-situ) is part of the mark.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: DDT sprayed on paddy kills stem borers but also honeybees visiting nearby mustard.  ·  Malathion runoff into a Terai pond kills fingerlings within days.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: DDT and BHC are persistent organochlorines; malathion degrades faster — persistence decides exam answers.  ·  Biomagnification explains why top predators suffer most even when water levels look low.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: [Remember] Pesticides are chemicals that kill pests: insecticides (insects), herbicides (weeds), fungicides (fungi), rodenticides (rats) — e.g. DDT, BHC, malathion, 2,4-D.  ·  [Remember] Effects on pests: target kill and crop protection; effects beyond target — killing of pollinators and predators, pest resurgence and resistance after repeated use.  ·  [Understand] Human-health effects: acute poisoning (nausea, tremor) and chronic effects (organ damage, suspected carcinogenicity); Terai farm workers face the highest exposure risk.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Pest resurgence happens because pesticides also kill predators — more spray can mean more pests later.  ·  IPM reduces but does not always eliminate chemicals; 'zero spray' is not the NEB definition.  ·  Do not swap the two sides of the contrast.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The example organism has to be able to do the job you assign it.  ·  Repeated spraying selects resistant pests, so the next generation is harder to kill.  ·  Define pesticide with its four classes and one example of each. **Answer.** **Pesticide:** a chemical used to kill or control pest organisms. 1. **Insecticide** — kills insects; e.g. DDT, malathion. 2. **Herbicide** — kills weeds; e.g. 2,4-D. 3. **Fungicide** — kills fungi; e.g. Bordeaux mixture. 4.…

rows.text: Sketch the biomagnification ladder (water → fish → bird) with rising concentration arrows. **Answer.** **Water** — DDT 0.000003 ppm (dilute) ↑ absorbed by **Aquatic plants/zooplankton** — 0.04 ppm ↑ eaten by small fish (each fish concentrates many meals) **Small fish** — 0.5 ppm ↑ eaten by large fish **Large fish** —…  ·  Recall card: class → target → non-target effect → one safe-use rule. **Answer.** **Class:** organochlorine insecticide (e.g. DDT). **Target:** chewing and sucking insects, mosquitoes. **Non-target effect:** persists for decades, biomagnifies up food chains, thins raptor eggshells, kills fish and bees.…  ·  IPM is the NEB-expected conclusion for every pesticide long answer.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  [Understand] Environmental effects: soil-microbe loss and fertility fall; water pollution and fish kills; biomagnification up food chains (classic case: DDT in birds); harm to bees and natural enemies.  ·  [Apply] Safe-use table — read label dose, wear protection, spray with wind direction, observe waiting period before harvest, never wash sprayers in ponds or rivers.
